Sikki Craft is a traditional handicraft from Bihar, especially associated with the Mithila region. It is made using sikki, a golden coloured grass that grows naturally in marshy areas. Artisans dry and dye the grass in vibrant colours.

They then weave and coil it around a base made of munj grass. This craft reflects the rich cultural heritage of Bihar and showcases the beauty of traditional handmade artistry.

In Dastkaari – The Craft of India, Episode 24 explores the traditional art of Mata Ni Pachedi from Gujarat with master artisan Roshan Chitara, a State Award–winning artist who continues a rich generational legacy. Mata Ni Pachedi is a sacred textile art form created on cotton fabric using natural colours and bamboo sticks instead of brushes. Originating within the Vaghari community, this art form depicts devotional stories of the Mother Goddess, along with mythological scenes and cultural traditions. The process involves preparing the cloth, creating natural dyes, and carefully hand-painting detailed compositions that reflect devotion, heritage, and storytelling. Set during the difficult time of the 1947 Partition, this film tells the heartbreaking true story of Boota Singh, a Sikh soldier, and Zainab, a Muslim girl. After Boota Singh rescues Zainab during the riots, the two fall in love and get married. They start a happy life together and have a daughter, showing that love can bring people together even when the world is divided by religion and war.

However, their happiness is cut short when the government forces Zainab to return to Pakistan. Refusing to be apart from his wife, Boota Singh takes a dangerous journey across the border to find her. Starring Gurdas Maan and Divya Dutta, this powerful drama shows the great sacrifices a person will make for love and the painful cost of borders and politics

Are migrants really welcomed back to their motherland? Is it the same motherland which they left behind? Does the motherland have the same rich, cultural values which they strove to teach to their children? Are they left confused about where they fit in? Could Love bloom within two young hearts, born and raised in two different lands? Does forgiveness and love calm the stormy ocean of human hearts? What does the West offer the East and what does the East offer the West? Is unity possible?
